findings: The answer leads with the key source-first conclusion that UTF-8 character count alone does not determine a unique byte size.
It gives concrete, reproducible ASCII/LF, ASCII/CRLF, three-byte/LF and three-byte/CRLF scenarios rather than hiding assumptions behind one number.
The five-point one-minute backbone is orally usable and separates formula, encoding width, newline width and final conclusion.
The Java estimator is explicitly scoped to homogeneous known byte widths and uses checked arithmetic; the fixture covers expected values and failure boundaries.
The answer distinguishes logical file bytes from filesystem allocation overhead, avoiding an unsupported storage-system assumption.
